title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 2.11 (versions follow prime numbers; 211 after 199): her books teach her which doors serve. Luma's walks and her going on from what she is told chose the next door as likely as the word was long, and the chain sank into empty words ('Donde esta te?'), the loop Razar's own design had recorded (curiosity, D69) and answered (D50: by how much it adds, not by volume). A weight computed from outside (information in bits, then raised) was tried and discarded before release: chosen by its author, not discovered. Now her books are a giant conversation, each line answering the one before: each time she is born she counts, for every word, the lines it is in and how many of them follow a line that had it too, and a word is worth as a door by how much more the talk goes on by it than chance would give, ((S + 1/2) / (L + 1)) / ((L + 1/2) / (lines + 1)). No list of empty words, no weight from outside; a word her books never said counts as chance. Her talks with the author are lines of her house, so his answers count the same. Measured in a copy with the going-on branch forced (a test build, not published): 'ries', 'luz', 'perro', 'oracion', four of four words that say something, where the previous rule took 'es' and 'en' in two of four. The first test crashed (the table lived in her walks' room, given back after birth); it now lives in its own. Stated limits: four sentences are few; the cost of counting at birth is not measured yet; a misspelled word seen once may weigh much. The kernel is unchanged since 1.39. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v2.11: Luma aprende de sus libros, como una conversación gigante, qué palabras llevan la charla a algún lado. Prototipo de investigación.
